Legs.Subject: FixedRateAccumulator.Integrate driven through Subjects.RateSchedule — twelve steps whose Int128 numerator, Int128.DivRem truncating quotient and retained signed remainder are the whole member
Legs.Against: Oracles.RateIntegrationLedger — the same schedule replayed in BigInteger with the division derived from the DEFINITION (magnitude quotient, sign re-applied, remainder by multiply-back) and NO checked cast anywhere, compared at EVERY STEP on both the advanced quantity and the retained remainder rather than only at the close

Legs.Subject: the ledger identity, checked at every PREFIX and not merely at the close: ticksPerSecond·Σ advanced + remainder equals Σ rate·ticks + the initial remainder, exactly, in BigInteger. This is the type's entire contract — that the discarded part is RETAINED rather than resolved — and it is the statement a rounding integrator would fail while still matching step-by-step magnitudes

the retained remainder never leaves (−ticksPerSecond, ticksPerSecond) at any step, including across the schedule's sign change where truncation toward zero flips its sign, so FromRemainder's admission band and Integrate's reachable band are the SAME band
a zero-tick step is a fixed point: it advances exactly zero and leaves the remainder bit-identical, which the schedule includes deliberately

an overflowing step is ATOMIC: where the exact quotient leaves the signed 64-bit range the member throws OverflowException and the accumulator's Remainder and TicksPerSecond are unchanged, so a caller that catches and retries is not silently one step ahead. The oracle carries NO checked cast, so the refusal is judged from outside the subject's own boundary

the construction refusal ladder: 0, −1, −65536 and long.MinValue are all refused by the constructor AND by FromRemainder with ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming the 'ticksPerSecond' parameter, while 1, 2, 60 and long.MaxValue are admitted and read back through TicksPerSecond unchanged with Remainder exactly zero

the default-initialized value is a distinct, LOUD state: default(FixedRateAccumulator) reports TicksPerSecond zero and Remainder zero, and Integrate throws InvalidOperationException rather than dividing by zero — the doc's explicit design choice, pinned

FromRemainder's admission band is exactly (−N, N): the remainders N−1, −(N−1) and 0 are admitted and round-trip through Remainder and TicksPerSecond, while N, −N and long.MaxValue are refused with ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming the 'remainder' parameter — the boundary tested from BOTH sides at each of Subjects.RateBaseLadder's nine bases

a restored accumulator CONTINUES the captured integration exactly, which is the doc's claim and not merely a field copy: running the tail of Subjects.RateSchedule against FromRemainder(r, N) reaches the same per-step advance as running the whole schedule against a fresh accumulator, at the step where its remainder was r, and closes on the same remainder

Reset clears the remainder and PRESERVES the base, and a reset accumulator integrates exactly as a fresh one does — while the ledger identity is deliberately broken across the reset, which is what makes Reset the documented teleport hook rather than a no-op

the documented headline — a constant rate advancing by exactly its own raw after ticksPerSecond one-tick calls — over Subjects.RateBaseLadder's bases at or below 1000, for the rate raws +2¹⁶ and −2¹⁶ and for the swept rate
Legs.Against: the ledger re-derived PER STEP in BigInteger from the accumulator's own invariant: carrying a remainder r in, the tick advances the truncation toward zero of (r + R)/N and retains (r + R) − N·that, so all N deltas and all N intermediate remainders are compared and not merely the closing pair. Summed, N·S + r_N = N·R with |r_N| < N forces S = R and r_N = 0 for either sign. The negative arm's asymmetry lives entirely in the middle — at N = 3 and R = −2¹⁶ the deltas are −21845, −21845, −21846 against the remainders −1, −2, 0 — and the law now ASSERTS those rather than describing them, which is what makes the truncating remainder's sign flip checked rather than narrated

Legs.Subject: the claim is about a rate that CANNOT be represented per tick, and the law says so: at the two ladder bases above 2¹⁶ the FIRST one-tick call at a one-unit-per-second rate advances exactly zero and retains the whole rate as the remainder, and every one of the thousand prefix steps then lands on the exact truncated quotient — so an implementation that dropped the tail would sit at zero forever instead of letting the unit arrive late

route agreement for a single-signed schedule: k one-tick calls at one rate reach the same TOTAL and the same closing remainder as one k-tick call at that rate, at k = N for the loopable bases and k = 1000 for the two large ones. ENVELOPE, stated rather than hidden: this is claimed for single-signed schedules ONLY — with mixed signs the two routes may differ by one raw, because truncation toward zero is not associative across a sign change, and rate.schedule-vs-ledger's prefix identity is what covers that case

an arbitrary swept rate closes the same way, and a bounded prefix of a billion-tick base is pinned exactly rather than approximately: after k one-tick calls at raw rate R the total advanced is the exact truncated quotient of k·R by N and the remainder is exactly the rest, in BigInteger, at every one of the thousand steps

Reset is exercised inside the closed turn: after the full N calls the accumulator's remainder is cleared and its base preserved, so the member is read at the one state where its 'preserve the base' half is distinguishable from constructing a fresh accumulator
FixedVector3RateAccumulator.Integrate over Subjects.RateSchedule, all three axes and all twelve steps
Legs.Against: Oracles.RateIntegrationLedger run three times — three independent exact BigInteger ledgers over the same schedule — compared at every step on each axis's advanced quantity and retained remainder

Legs.Subject: FixedVector3RateAccumulator.Integrate's three axes
Legs.Against: three separate FixedRateAccumulator instances driven with the same schedule and the same base
Legs.Shared: FixedRateAccumulator.IntegrateRaw — the IDENTICAL internal member on both sides, not a sibling copy (FixedRateAccumulator.cs:198-215 against 80-85) — so agreement proves the fan-out and never the arithmetic
Legs.Citation: the classical leg above, which runs the exact ledger IN THIS CASE on the same operands, and rate.schedule-vs-ledger, which pins IntegrateRaw through the scalar face

Legs.Subject: the three axes never cross-contaminate: a schedule that drives one axis alone leaves the other two remainders exactly zero and returns exactly zero on those components at every step, checked for each of the three in turn — which is what 'three independent axes' means and which a shared accumulator field would break

the four reset members are exactly as selective as their names: ResetX clears XRemainder and leaves YRemainder, ZRemainder and TicksPerSecond bit-identical, likewise ResetY and ResetZ, and Reset clears all three while preserving the base — checked from a state whose three remainders are DISTINCT and non-zero, so a transposed field fails here

Integrate is ATOMIC across axes: when the Z axis's quotient overflows the member throws OverflowException and NONE of the three remainders has advanced — because all three steps are computed before any is written — so a caught overflow leaves a coherent vector state rather than a torn one
the default-initialized vector accumulator throws InvalidOperationException from Integrate and reports TicksPerSecond zero, exactly as its scalar sibling does

the construction refusal ladder matches the scalar sibling's exactly: 0, −1, −65536 and long.MinValue are refused by the constructor and by FromRemainders with ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming 'ticksPerSecond', and an admitted base leaves all three remainders exactly zero

FromRemainders refuses when ANY axis's magnitude reaches the base, tested one axis at a time at each of the nine ladder bases so all three validation calls are reached, and admits the boundary triple (N−1, 0, −(N−1)), round-tripping all four readers

every FromRemainders refusal NAMES THE FAILING AXIS by that axis's own parameter — an out-of-band X reports 'xRemainder', a Y reports 'yRemainder', a Z reports 'zRemainder' — each axis probed alone at every one of the nine ladder bases and each asserted against its OWN expected name, so a copy-pasted parameter name, a transposed argument or a re-used scalar validator fails here. A caller restoring a snapshot can therefore tell which axis was rejected, which the shared 'remainder' name could not say

the axes are validated in X, Y, Z order and the refusal reports the FIRST axis out of band, which is what the member's <exception> tag states: with all three axes out of band the refusal names 'xRemainder', and with Y and Z out of band it names 'yRemainder' — checked at every ladder base, so a reordered or short-circuited validation sequence is visible

a restored vector accumulator continues each axis's captured integration exactly, checked by replaying the tail of Subjects.RateSchedule against FromRemainders of the three remainders the full run reached at that step and requiring the same per-step vector and the same closing triple
